Huaylas was an Andean people and chiefdom of the Callejón de Huaylas, the valley of the Santa River in the Ancash region of Peru. In 1492 it was part of the Inca Empire. Earlier the valley had been home to the Recuay culture, and the great temple of Chavín stood just across the mountains to the east.

The Incas bound Huaylas to them by marriage. The emperor Huayna Capac took Contarhuacho, daughter of a Huaylas lord, as a wife. Their daughter Quispe Sisa, baptised Inés Huaylas Yupanqui, became the partner of Francisco Pizarro after the conquest, and Huaylas lords sent help to the Spanish during the Inca siege of Lima in 1536.

The people of the valley still speak a local Quechua. In 1970 an earthquake set off an avalanche from Huascarán that buried the town of Yungay.
